---
title: "Scenarios"
---

A scenario is one workflow of an open source project that you play from start to end. Each step has a learning goal and a question for your learning notebook.

## Your first contribution

You are a newcomer to [tinystats](https://github.com/florence-bockting/tinystats), a small Python package for statistics. You choose an issue, fix it and get your pull request merged.

| | |
| :-- | :-- |
| Duration | About 2 hours |
| Your role | Newcomer |

### Learning goals

| ID | Goal |
| :-- | :-- |
| G1 | Set up the environment |
| G2 | Understand the project structure |
| G3 | Make a change that follows the contribution guidelines |
| G4 | Respond to review |

### Steps

| Step | You do | Goal |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| 0 | Set up the environment. Run the tests. | G1 |
| 1 | Explore the project. Answer three questions about its structure. | G2 |
| 2 | Choose an issue. Write a comment that you want to work on it. | G3 |
| 3 | Create a branch. Fix the issue. Add a test and a line to the changelog. | G3 |
| 4 | Push the branch. Open a pull request. | G3 |
| 5 | Read each review comment. Answer each comment. | G4 |
| 6 | Push one commit for each requested change. | G4 |
| 7 | Write your final reflection after the merge. | G1–G4 |

### Roles

| Role | Played by |
| :-- | :-- |
| Newcomer | You |
| Fellow contributor | A peer, else an LLM |
| Maintainer | A peer, else an LLM |
| Reviewer | A peer, else an LLM |
| CI bot | A script |

### Rules

1. A peer fills each role first. An LLM fills a role only when no peer is available.
2. Each message from an LLM has a mark that shows it comes from an LLM.
3. The LLM can explain or help you write a draft. Only peers and mentors give the feedback that counts.
4. The LLM never writes the fix for you.

## Future scenarios

- You are the reviewer
- You are the maintainer
- You are the release manager
- You handle a difficult discussion
